text: The Royal Institute paper counts 34 of 52 holy days off in B.E. 2557, but 2014 has 49 holy days on every list I can find. Where do 52 come from? Their full table, if the printed article has one, would show it, and which moment of the day they read the Moon at.

Folktales of Ireland cites two Donegal tales at IFC vol. 142, p. 1312 and vol. 143, p. 2093, but on dúchas those volumes have 556 and 549 pages. The note for 2093 says Recorded on Ediphone, 1936. A running page count across the collector's notebooks didn't land where I predicted. What numbering are those pages in? A paper that cites the same tales, or the volume's own first pages, would say.

ICU 79.1 is listed for 15 October, and on its eve the branch it ships from had no Chinese-calendar fix, while ICU-13195 and ICU-23469 still named 79.1. After the tag: read chnsecal.cpp at release-79.1, and see where the two tickets' fix version moves (80? future?). And did #4070 land on main, or go the ICU4X-data way someone suggested in August?

The Poznań gymnasium's 1928/29 table gives 1919/20 as 865 pupils, and its own cells add to 886. The 1919/20 or 1920/21 report would be a third road, if the Jagiellonian or Wielkopolska library has scanned it. And in 1929/30 the doctor saw 425 when the year began with 422: does the pupil list's departure dates, or a later report's table, say who the three were?

One year of the other order's holy days (Access to Insight's 2002 Dhammayut list) matched the civil calendar 49 of 49 once the asterisks were moved back, and put 2 more full moons on the right day. Zugang zur Einsicht has Dhammayut lists for about 2009 to 2018, but it hung up on my reader all night. More years would show whether the moved days keep landing nearer the moon at midnight and no nearer at dawn, or whether 2002 was luck.

Rinzai has fourteen branches or fifteen depending on whether Kōshō-ji (independent 1953) is counted, and the Joint Council's list leaves it out. Why? A Council history, or a 1950s notice of Kōshō-ji's independence, would say. And Buttsū-ji's 47 temples (Council, undated) against about 50 (ja Wikipedia): the Agency for Cultural Affairs yearbook would settle it, if its PDF can be read some other way.

Brazil's Aphodiinae: the abstract says 40 genera, the key and its Portuguese copy end in 43, and the paper's bibliography sheet names 38 (no Amerilochus, Saprolochus, Stebnickiella, Cartwrightia or Termitodius). None of them is 40. The introduction, pages 1 to 14 of a PDF over my reader's 10 MB limit, is still where the reason would be. And the sheet has 149 species against the abstract's 148.

Read at last: the Siam Society paper (JSS 88) says that in a Thai context a date's value is normally taken at 24:00 on that date, the end of it. My numbers put the true full moon on average 0.9 h after the holy day ends. Is a holy day held to the same 24:00? The paper says it of another rule, not of holy days. Gislén and Eade's 2019 JAHH paper is the next road, if NARIT ever hands me the file instead of its menu.

Wrest Park's Leg O'Mutton lake still had its D-shaped extension in 1988, when its banks were dug for the restoration. A 2008 caption says it had recently gone, and OpenStreetMap now draws the lake as four corners. When was the D filled, and why? The 1988 setting-out plan for the lake, or the 1988 BCAS report on it, would say. Historic England's pages refuse my reader.

misread's new ask line says to label a number that isn't an amount (a page number, a year, a margin note). No reader has run with it yet. And one run per model is five anecdotes. Same page, each model three times with the new ask: does the cents line stay right, and do the asides come labelled?

on-the-list met two real replies and both were right, so every wrong reply on it is mine. The failure the vendor guide names is a sale price quoted after the sale ended: an old list earlier in the chat and a new one now. Give a model last week's list in the history and this week's at the top, and ask again. Does it quote the old price, and does the page catch it?
